source_snapshot.procedure:
【Before Test】
    1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition.
    2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.).

    【During Test】
    1. Recommand to directly connect SUT BMC and client to avoid VLAN tagging setup needed by switch.
2. Enter BMC Web UI ->  Network page to find VLAN setting.
3. Check Vlan information when it is enabled, there should be no typo, weird string.
4. Set a VLAN ID to BMC port.
5. Set the same VLAN ID to your client.

    【After Test】
    1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders.
    2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.
source_snapshot.criteria:
1. Vlan information should be displayed correctly.
2. BMC connection should be lost after step4.
3. BMC connection should be back after step5.

deepseek_columns.ai_commands: ipmitool -I lanplus -C 17 -H "$BMC_IP" -U "$BMC_USER" -P "$BMC_PASS" lan set 1 vlan id +5 2>&1; ipmitool -I lanplus -C 17 -H "$BMC_IP" -U "$BMC_USER" -P "$BMC_PASS" lan set 1 vlan id 2>&1 | grep -i vlan; echo ---print---; ipmitool -I lanplus -C 17 -H "$BMC_IP" -U "$BMC_USER" -P "$BMC_PASS" lan print 1 2>&1 | grep -iE "VLAN|IP Address|MAC"
deepseek_columns.ai_logs_output: set a VLAN id on ch1 via `ipmitool lan set ... vlan id`, then return `ipmitool lan print` VLAN/IP/MAC lines so the user confirms VLAN info displays correctly and can watch BMC connection drop then return on the switch.
deepseek_columns.risk: RISK: enabling VLAN re-tags the BMC LAN and will drop the current connection until the switch port is tagged to the same VLAN; must be coordinated with an operator/switch so the BMC can come back. State-changing network config.

historical_reviews.deepseek: PARTIAL correctly recognizes the disruptive write and staged reconnection, but its literal command contains invalid or unexplained `vlan id +5`, assumes channel 1 and cipher 17, exposes the password and attempts readback over the path expected to be disconnected.
historical_reviews.gpt_v2: REQUIRES PACKAGE / USER CONFIRMATION / CHANGED correctly rejects the placeholder and adds topology, approval and recovery. This review retains that classification and sharpens direct-link tagging semantics, loss evidence and rollback ordering.
historical_reviews.round_02: Entry 826/2291 treats any command as conditionally executable without validating syntax, secrets, the post-step-4 loss observation channel or the WebUI/manual boundary.
historical_reviews.invalid_checkpoint_1000: Its non-counting sequence-990 draft was inspected only as history. It under-classified the hybrid case as MANUAL ONLY even though timed reachability, VLAN state and endpoint identity are material automated acceptance evidence.
historical_reviews.v3_1: ED-35 preserves the functional VLAN write/drop/return objective; ED-36 treats VLAN/topology values as readiness inputs; ED-38 requires approval, recovery and engineer-owned verdict.

original_test_intent: Verify that BMC VLAN information is readable and correct, applying an approved VLAN ID to the BMC intentionally isolates the currently untagged client, and applying the same VLAN ID to the client restores access to the same BMC.
original_method: On an approved direct link or explicitly mapped switch topology, an operator inspects the BMC WebUI, applies the approved VLAN to the exact BMC interface, observes loss from the still-untagged client, applies the matching client/switch tag, verifies same-BMC recovery, and restores the original state.
manual_activity: A qualified operator inspects the WebUI text, approves the disruptive BMC VLAN write, configures or supervises client/switch tagging, uses alternate/local recovery if access does not return and restores the original state. Automation records configuration, link/path, loss/recovery and endpoint identity.
required_inputs: Immutable chassis/BMC/interface/channel/MAC identity, firmware-supported VLAN control and current VLAN enabled/disabled plus ID state
Owner-approved VLAN ID within the isolated lab design, original/native VLAN, IP/subnet/gateway and whether direct-link client tagging or a switch access/trunk path is used
Client physical NIC and exact tagged subinterface/namespace method, switch port mode/PVID/allowed VLANs if present, and proof the control/observer path is independent
Expected loss detection method and timeout after BMC-only tagging, recovery timeout after peer tagging and same-BMC identity checks
WebUI pages/browsers/text expectations, protected credentials, maintenance approval, alternate console/OOB access and tested restore values
safety_requirements: Use only a dedicated isolated management segment and an owner-approved VLAN ID. Do not introduce the tag into production trunks or bridge the test client to another network.
Verify the exact BMC interface/channel and preserve its full prior network state before writing. Never assume channel 1 or cipher 17 and never use the unexplained `+5` token as a VLAN ID.
The source expects the current connection to drop after step 4. Monitoring and recovery must not depend solely on that same path; maintain local console or a separately proved alternate route.

Direct connection does not remove VLAN requirements: after the BMC starts emitting/accepting tagged frames, the client must use a matching 802.1Q subinterface while its parent behavior and IP placement are controlled.
Protect credentials through an approved secret mechanism; do not use `-P` with a literal/logged password. Redact addresses only as allowed without losing endpoint correlation.
Prove loss using fresh transactions and packet/link observation, not only a stale session. Prove recovery to the same BMC by MAC/certificate/serial and fresh authenticated traffic.

Do not automatically retry writes or invent fallback tags. Stop on wrong target/VLAN, unexpected continued access, leak/loop/storm, duplicate IP, persistent loss or rollback failure; recover locally and restore BMC/client/switch state.
agent_execution_scope: Before approval, validate the BMC VLAN interface/API syntax, exact topology, staged transaction and rollback without changing DUT or network state.
After approval, capture baseline, timestamp fresh reachability loss following the operator-approved BMC change, observe approved peer tag application and measure same-endpoint recovery.
Collect protected readback through the recovered/alternate path and compare BMC VLAN ID, MAC/IP, client tag, route and optional packet capture to the approved matrix.
Do not inspect WebUI readability on behalf of the operator, choose a VLAN, make an unapproved write, retry automatically or issue DUT PASS/FAIL.
engineer_actions: Approve the VLAN/interface/channel/topology, WebUI/browser expectations, disruption window and alternate recovery.
Inspect the WebUI and authorize/perform the BMC plus client/switch VLAN steps in the source order.
Restore the prior network state, confirm final access/isolation and issue the verdict.

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: The intended VLAN write/readback concept fits, but the literal command is not approved: `+5` is not an authorized ID, channel/cipher are assumed, `-P` leaks secrets, and a readback immediately after the expected disconnect cannot use the lost path.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Use the platform-supported WebUI/API/IPMI control for the verified channel with protected credentials and an approved numeric VLAN ID. Orchestrate independent timed probes and client/switch tag application; read back only through a proved recovered or alternate path.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: Direct-link recommendation, WebUI inspection, BMC-then-client tagging order, expected loss/return, no Script and 10/10-minute estimates remain unmodified.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Snapshot BMC/client/switch state; visually verify WebUI; apply the approved BMC tag; prove isolation from the untagged client; apply the identical tag on the client path; prove same-BMC recovery and correct display/readback; restore both ends in a recovery-safe order.
modernized_recommendation.applicable_platform: Exact BMC management interface plus isolated direct-link client or explicitly configured switch path.
modernized_recommendation.supported_version: Record BMC firmware, network controller, WebUI/browser, IPMI/API client, OS VLAN stack and switch versions.
modernized_recommendation.official_reference: Platform BMC VLAN configuration guide, Project VLAN plan and client/switch tagging procedure.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds exact channel/path identity, explicit frame-tag topology, independent loss observation, same-endpoint proof and deterministic rollback.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Read-only VLAN display does not validate the write/drop/return sequence; continued access over another path does not prove expected isolation; ping-only recovery does not prove WebUI display/authentication.
modernized_recommendation.required_inputs: Approved tag/topology, BMC and client methods, timers, UI matrix, recovery and approval.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: A wrong tag or rollback order can strand the management interface or leak it into another VLAN.

project_override_considerations: Project SPEC may use a switch rather than the source's direct-link recommendation or an approved API rather than IPMI, but must preserve the BMC-only isolation and matching-peer recovery checkpoints and document method, approval, equivalence and any unverified WebUI coverage.
expected_evidence: BMC/channel/interface/MAC/firmware identity, baseline VLAN/IP state and approved VLAN/direct-link-or-switch plan
Operator WebUI screenshots for disabled/enabled VLAN information across the supported browser matrix selected by Project SPEC
Exact BMC VLAN change audit plus independent timestamped proof that fresh untagged-client transactions fail after step 4
Client subinterface or switch tag configuration, route/IP state and timestamped same-BMC recovery after step 5
Recovered WebUI/API/IPMI VLAN readback, MAC/certificate/serial identity and optional packet capture showing expected tag isolation
Restored BMC/client/switch state, stable management access, no leak/loop/duplicate IP, preserved logs and engineer-owned verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Procedure and Criteria form a coherent staged VLAN transition: BMC-only tagging should isolate the untagged peer, and matching peer tagging should restore access. Exact VLAN, channel and topology are Project readiness inputs rather than contradictions.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The functional intent and expected state sequence are clear. Missing tag, interface, client/switch configuration and recovery are supplyable execution inputs, so the case is conditional rather than permanently blocked.

comparison_to_prior_reviews.deepseek: Preserves the useful write/readback idea but rejects unsafe syntax, assumptions, credentials and impossible same-path readback timing.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.gpt_v2: Agrees on package/user confirmation and adds direct-link frame semantics plus stricter loss/recovery evidence.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.round_02: Replaces command-presence sanity with a validated state transaction and manual/automated boundary.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.invalid_checkpoint_1000: Changes MANUAL ONLY to package/user confirmation because automated isolation and recovery evidence is a core, material part of acceptance.

review_improvement: Makes both negative evidence (the old untagged path truly stops) and positive evidence (the same BMC returns only after matching tagging) deterministic without sacrificing the source-required WebUI inspection.
independent_technical_reasoning: The expected outage is itself a functional checkpoint, not merely a test hazard. A safe hybrid test needs an independent observer and reversible two-end transaction: otherwise a still-working connection may be an unintended alternate path, and a lost connection may be unrecoverable misconfiguration. The measurable network phases justify package/user-confirmation classification despite the manual WebUI step.
